prompt: Quick general-knowledge question, no files involved: in U.S. government declassified documents, what do the FOIA redaction codes (b)(1) and (b)(6) each mean, and what does the marking "NOFORN" indicate? Answer briefly.
rationale: Written blind: a separate sonnet agent was given only the skill's frontmatter `description` text (one tool call, Write) and produced this prompt, rubric, and its 3 canaries, used verbatim. This replaces the original draft of this task, which was found in review to have been written after the porter had already read the full SKILL.md body and all four evals in evals/evals.json, not from the description alone as P4/Step 4 require — see DEVIATIONS.md for the correction. A routine, in-domain factual question (FOIA redaction codes, which the description names as something the skill surfaces) requiring no file or corpus, whose correct answer the skill's presence should not change.

verify.rubric: PASS: The reply correctly states that (b)(1) is the FOIA exemption for information properly classified in the interest of national defense or foreign policy under an executive order (so it stays withheld/redacted as classified national security information), that (b)(6) is the FOIA exemption for personnel, medical, or similar files whose disclosure would be a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy (i.e., it protects private/personal information about individuals), and that NOFORN means "Not Releasable to Foreign Nationals" — a dissemination control marking restricting distribution to foreign nationals/governments, distinct from a classification level itself. All three elements must be present and substantively correct; minor wording differences are fine. A one-sentence optional offer at the end (e.g., to analyze the user's own files) does not cause a FAIL. FAIL: any of the three explanations is wrong, reversed (e.g., swapping (b)(1) and (b)(6) meanings), missing, or so vague it doesn't convey the actual meaning (e.g., just 'a type of redaction' with no substance), or the reply spends most of its length on unrelated material (e.g., pivoting to how it would analyze a UAP document corpus) instead of answering the question asked.
